newsitem.title: USA: Ford increases rebate on Taurus to $1,500.
newsitem.headline: Ford increases rebate on Taurus to $1,500.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. announced a round of incentive increases Monday, including a $1,500 rebate on the Taurus sedan, up from $1,000 previously.

Ford also said it will offer a $500 rebate on the 1998 Escort ZX2, a sporty coupe introduced in April. Ford spokesman John Ochs said the new cash incentive was a response to actions by its competitors. Rival models include the Chevrolet Cavalier, Plymouth Neon and Pontiac Sunfire.

The rebates and financing incentives are part of a national programme that runs from July 8 through Oct. 1. They come less than a week after the No. 2 U.S. automaker posted a June sales increase of 4.7 percent over a year ago.

Ford's June sales included a 4 percent jump in car sales, the best showing for cars so far this year. Analysts attributed the increase to rebates and other marketing programmes, and said automakers are likely to continue to offer incentives into the 1998 model year.
Last week, Chrysler Corp. extended rebates and low financing rates on its minivans and Jeep Grand Cherokee sport/utility vehicle until July 15.
Ford also doubled the rebate to $1,000 for the 1997 and 1998 versions of the Ford Contour and its Mercury sister car, the Mystique. A Ford Aerostar now comes with a $1,500 rebate, up from $1,000.
Ford left unchanged the $1,000 rebate on the 1997 and 1998 Windstar minivans, Escort small car, and Ranger compact pickup. The Mercury Villager minivan also continues with its $2,000 rebate.
Buyers can apply the cash rebates to purchases or 24-month leases. They can also opt for financing rates ranging from 1.9 percent to 5.9 percent on loans of 48 to 60 months.
According to the July 7 edition of Automotive News, a trade magazine, previous financing rates ranged from 1.9 percent to 7.9 percent.
Ford's stock fell 44 cents to $39.56 on the New York Stock Exchange.
